name: Bricks Game
description: Use arrow keys or the mouse to move the paddle. Use space to restart. This shader uses the new Multipass system
license: Original header: 'Created by inigo quilez - iq/2016', Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0. Verbatim reference passes are preserved here unmodified for provenance and A/B validation; the shipped app is a faithful C++ port of the same algorithm and constants.

inputs.note: Declared as an input but never sampled by the Image source; no audio path exists in soft3d, so it is unused.

adaptation: The engine has no render-to-texture (all FBO entry points in libs/gles/src/gles2/gles2_api.c are name-only stubs), textures are RGBA8-only (portablegl pglTextureImage2D rejects non-GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE/non-GL_RGBA), and the CPU GLSL interpreter has no texelFetch. Buffer A self-references its previous frame, so it cannot be flattened into one GL pass, and its float game state (ball position, brick hit-times = iTime) cannot survive an RGBA8 texture. The faithful, all-targets path is therefore a direct C++ port: Buffer A's gameplay is run literally per texel over the 14x14 state grid with prev/curr float buffers (identical read-old/write-new ordering, iFrame reset, 3-substep swept collisions, keyboard/mouse paddle drive), and the Image distance-field renderer runs per output pixel with a lossless per-frame brick table precompute (doBrick depends only on brick id and iTime). All constants, hash functions, SDF primitives, glow/shadow terms, score glyphs and the game-over tint are preserved verbatim. CPU-composited into an 0xAARRGGBB buffer and presented as a fullscreen textured quad (the matrix/Fireworks idiom). Mouse-hold steers the paddle, arrow keys move it, space restarts, ESC quits.
